pharm: Oral immunoregulatory antirheumatic agent (4-acetamidophenylacetic acid) that suppresses pro-inflammatory cytokine production and lymphocyte adhesion in rheumatoid synovium
quick: 100 mg orally three times daily (300 mg/day) after meals
Caution; can cause proteinuria/nephrotic syndrome - monitor and reduce/avoid in impairment
Urinalysis (proteinuria), CBC, liver enzymes, respiratory symptoms
summary: Actarit (4-acetamidophenylacetic acid) is an oral immunomodulatory disease-modifying antirheumatic drug (DMARD) used in Japan and some Asian countries for rheumatoid arthritis, often as a slow-acting second-line agent and sometimes combined with methotrexate. The usual dose is 100 mg three times daily (300 mg/day) taken after meals. It modulates T-cell- and macrophage-driven synovial inflammation by suppressing TNF-alpha and IL-1beta secretion and down-regulating adhesion molecules rather than by inhibiting cyclooxygenase. Its signature toxicity is renal: it can cause proteinuria progressing to nephrotic syndrome and membranous nephropathy, similar to other Japanese DMARDs such as bucillamine and D-penicillamine, so regular urinalysis is essential. It is not FDA-approved. Clinical benefit develops slowly over weeks to months.
indications: Rheumatoid arthritis (slow-acting/second-line DMARD; sometimes in combination with methotrexate in refractory disease)

dosage.d: 100 mg orally three times daily (300 mg/day)
dosage.n: Slow-acting; benefit develops over weeks to months

dosage.d: 100 mg three times daily added to methotrexate
dosage.n: Intensify monitoring of marrow, renal and hepatic function

admin: Counsel that this is a slow-acting DMARD - benefit takes weeks to months and it is not a rescue analgesic
Perform baseline and periodic urinalysis for proteinuria
Monitor complete blood count and liver enzymes during therapy
Watch for respiratory symptoms suggestive of interstitial lung disease
Stop the drug if significant proteinuria or nephrotic syndrome develops
moa: Actarit is an immunomodulatory DMARD with several complementary actions rather than a simple anti-prostaglandin effect. At therapeutic concentrations it suppresses spontaneous secretion of TNF-alpha and IL-1beta by rheumatoid synovial cells; it down-regulates adhesion molecules including CD44 and ICAM-1 on fibroblast-like synoviocytes and VLA-4 on macrophage-like synovial cells, thereby reducing lymphocyte adhesion to synovium; and it lowers serum nitric oxide concentrations in correlation with clinical improvement. It has also been characterized as an inhibitor of carbonic anhydrase II. The net effect is modulation of the T-cell/macrophage-driven synovial inflammation of rheumatoid arthritis.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to actarit or excipients
relative: Significant renal impairment or existing proteinuria/nephrotic syndrome

preg: The safety of actarit in pregnancy has not been established. As an immunomodulatory DMARD it should be avoided in pregnancy unless clearly necessary; no formal pregnancy category is assigned in the available labeling.
lact: Use during breastfeeding is not recommended because safety in lactation has not been established.
renal: Use with caution in renal impairment. Actarit and its metabolites are excreted predominantly by the kidneys, and the drug itself can cause renal injury (proteinuria, nephrotic syndrome, membranous nephropathy). Reduce or avoid in significant renal impairment and monitor urine protein and renal function closely; discontinue if significant proteinuria develops.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment, as hepatic enzyme elevation has been reported. Monitor liver enzymes; no quantified dose-reduction schedule is published in the accessible labeling.

major: Other nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, iodinated contrast, ciclosporin) - additive renal injury risk
Other myelosuppressive DMARDs - additive hematologic toxicity
moderate: Methotrexate - commonly co-administered in refractory RA; requires intensified marrow, renal and hepatic monitoring
interactions.food: Take after meals; this is the standard administration and helps tolerability.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid or limit alcohol given the potential for hepatotoxicity and GI upset.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor urinalysis (proteinuria), complete blood count and liver enzymes during therapy.

serious: Proteinuria progressing to nephrotic syndrome / membranous nephropathy

monitoring: Urinalysis for proteinuria at baseline and periodically (key safety check)
Respiratory symptoms for interstitial lung disease
counsel: This medicine works slowly - it may take weeks to months to ease your joint symptoms; keep taking it as prescribed
Keep your urine and blood test appointments - they check for kidney and blood effects
Report frothy urine, ankle swelling, marked tiredness, fever, sore throat, or unusual bruising
Report a persistent cough, breathlessness or fever, which could signal a lung reaction
pk: Slow DMARD effect; measurable improvement over about 8-20 weeks depending on disease stage
Plasma peak within a few hours of an oral dose
Supports three-times-daily dosing; clinical effect accrues with continued use
Store at room temperature, protect from moisture and light
pearls: NOT FDA-approved - a Japan-origin immunomodulatory DMARD (also used in some Asian markets/India)
Signature toxicity is renal: watch for proteinuria progressing to nephrotic syndrome/membranous nephropathy (class effect shared with bucillamine and D-penicillamine)
Routine urinalysis is essential; stop on significant proteinuria
Slow-acting - counsel patients that benefit takes weeks to months; it is not an analgesic
Often combined with methotrexate in refractory rheumatoid arthritis
missed: Take the missed dose when you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your usual schedule - do not take a double dose.
overdose: There is no specific antidote. Provide supportive and symptomatic care, monitor renal function, blood counts and liver enzymes, and manage gastrointestinal symptoms. Consult a poison control center.
